question: Can the qualified raw-byte motif and adaptive-granularity stack learn a second hierarchy level that captures morphology-like compounds and a sealed long-range reference relation, improving compositional held-out prediction while preserving bounded state and event reduction without an external tokenizer?
hypothesis: Across four new seeds, a fixed-capacity hierarchy learned only from raw bytes will recover all eight qualified four-byte motifs plus four recurring two-motif compounds, achieve at least 0.95 held-out local successor accuracy and 0.90 long-range reference accuracy on unseen compound/reference combinations, reduce effective events by at least 0.30, outperform a motif-only ablation on long-range references by at least 0.50, and keep total learned structures at or below 16.

frozen_design.heldout_rule: one deterministic compound-A/compound-B/reference-parity family per seed is excluded from training and used for evaluation
frozen_design.learner_input: concatenated raw bytes only; no record, motif, compound, or semantic boundary labels

classification_rules.supported: All frozen thresholds and validity criteria pass.
classification_rules.mixed: Hierarchy is causal and improves held-out reference prediction but at least one accuracy, event-reduction, or capacity threshold fails.
classification_rules.negative: Validity passes but hierarchy provides less than 0.10 long-range gain or fails sealed-combination generalization.
classification_rules.incomplete: Environmental or compute interruption prevents frozen cardinality.
classification_rules.invalid: Provenance, hidden-boundary isolation, capacity, deterministic construction, or qualification isolation fails.

no_post_result_tuning_rule: Do not alter frozen inputs, capacities, metrics, thresholds, aggregation, or classification after observing output.
